name: Southern Betsimisaraka Malagasy (Retired)
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

sources.citation: Ferrand, Gabriel. 1909. Essai de phonétique comparée du malais et des dialectes malgaches. Paris: Paul Geuthner.
sources.note: Ch. VI 'L'accent tonique' (pp. 236-245) is a general Malagasy (Merina-based) statement: 'Les thèmes radicaux trisyllabiques sont généralement proparoxytons, quelquefois paroxytons, très rarement oxytons... Les thèmes radicaux disyllabiques sont généralement paroxytons, très rarement oxytons... Tous les monosyllabes sont accentués'; suffixes shift the accent one syllable right; reduplications/compounds keep the accent only on the last element. No dialect-specific statement; Betsimisaraka Sud is only listed among the dialects (p. XXXVIII) and appears in isolated accent-marked forms (e.g. 'Betsi…

sources.citation: Bulletin de l'Académie malgache, 1908 volume (Google/University of Michigan scan).
sources.note: Only volume of the Bulletin found on archive.org; contains no Betsimisaraka or Tesaka dialect article (Elle 1905 and Ruud 1955 are in other volumes, not found online).

sources.citation: [Webber, J.-B. et al.] 1855. Grammaire malgache rédigée par les missionnaires catholiques de Madagascar. Ile Bourbon: Etablissement malgache de Notre-Dame de la Ressource.
sources.note: Sec. 8 'De l'accent': 'Chaque mot a sa force dans une voyelle longue que l'on peut marquer d'un accent aigu... Négliger ou changer la longue, c'est changer de mot' (famòrana vs famoràna, tànana vs tanàna); sec. 48 'La racine primitive a l'accent sur la première syllabe'; a note that the accent-shift rule 'est invariable chez les Hovas, mais dans les Provinces, le peuple fait quelquefois passer l'accent sur cette demi-muette'. General Malagasy (Hova-based), not a Betsimisaraka statement.

sources.citation: Wikipedia, 'Malagasy language' (Phonology: Stress) and 'Southern Betsimisaraka Malagasy' (accessed 2026-09-17 via the MediaWiki API).
sources.note: General Malagasy only: 'Words are generally accented on the penultimate syllable, unless the word ends in ka, tra and often na, in which case they are stressed on the antepenultimate syllable' (uncited, not dialect-specific). The Southern Betsimisaraka page has no phonology section (geography and a 23-item vocabulary only).

sources.citation: Serva, Maurizio & Michele Pasquini. 2020. Dialects of Madagascar. PLoS ONE 15(10): e0240170.
sources.note: Lexicostatistical dialectometry (includes Betsimisaraka Sud and Antesaka wordlists); silent on stress.

sources.citation: O'Neill, Timothy. 2015. The phonology of Betsimisaraka Malagasy. PhD dissertation, University of Delaware (Vavatenina variety = Northern Betsimisaraka).
sources.note: Grep of the full text: no mention of Southern Betsimisaraka, 'Betsimisaraka du Sud', Ruud, Mananjary, Nosy Varika, Vatomandry or Mahanoro; its penultimate-default statement (ch. 5, p. 114) is already carried in the catalog under nort2890 and does not cover bzc/tkg.

sources.citation: Serva, M., F. Petroni, D. Volchenkov & S. Wichmann. 2012. The settlement of Madagascar: what dialects and languages can tell us. PLoS ONE 7(2): e30666.

ISO 639-3 Registration Authority. 2010. Change Request 2010-035: split [bjq]; create [bzc] Southern Betsimisaraka Malagasy and [tkg] Tesaka Malagasy (adopted 2011-05-18). Dallas: SIL International, 5 pp.
sources.note: Nothing on stress; identity and lexical-similarity argument only (Tesaka 70-80% with Official Malagasy, 76% Tanosy, 78% Betsimisaraka); cites Deschamps 1934/1936/1959, Kottak 1980, Bouwer 2010.

sources.citation: Jully, Antony. 1901. Manuel des dialectes malgaches comprenant sept dialectes: hova, betsileo, tankarana, betsimisaraka, taimorona, tanosy, sakalava (Mahafaly) et le soahely. Paris: J. André.
sources.note: Comparative vocabulary only; the 'Accentuation' note explains a notation (italic syllable = pronounced with a pause and more strongly) applied across the seven dialects; no rule for Betsimisaraka and no indication which Betsimisaraka.

sources.citation: Sibree, James (transl., ed.). 'The manners and customs, superstitions and dialect of the Betsimisaraka; Part I' (translated from a Hova evangelist's MS). The Antananarivo Annual and Madagascar Magazine vol. IV (nos. 13-16, 1889-1892), pp. 67-75.
sources.note: Concerns the interior Betsimisaraka west of Mahanoro (Southern Betsimisaraka territory); 'Their dialect and way of speaking' (pp. 74-75) gives lexical and sandhi remarks (ha/he/hi/ho > tra/tre/tri/tro; n > velar nasal) but nothing on accent or stress. Other AA volumes: no Betsimisaraka accent statement found by grep.

sources.citation: Ruud, Jørgen. 1955. Étude grammaticale du dialecte Betsimisaraka du Sud. Bulletin de l'Académie Malgache n.s. 33: 33-55.
